settings.question: How soon will I see a difference?
settings.answer: Most people notice better tone and hydration within two to three weeks. Collagen changes are slower — plan on eight to twelve weeks of consistent use before judging it. That is why the trial runs 60 nights rather than 30.

settings.question: Is it safe for sensitive or darker skin?
settings.answer: Yes. Red and near-infrared light carry no UV and generate almost no heat, so there is no melanin-related risk — it is safe across all Fitzpatrick types. If you are on photosensitising medication such as isotretinoin or doxycycline, check with your doctor first.

settings.question: How often should I use it?
settings.answer: Five sessions a week, ten minutes each. More than one session a day does not speed anything up — the tissue response saturates, and consistency matters far more than intensity.

settings.question: Do I need goggles?
settings.answer: No. The eye openings use recessed optics and built-in opaque shields, so no light reaches the eye directly. Keep your eyes closed during a session anyway, out of habit.

settings.question: What if it does not work for me?
settings.answer: Send it back within 60 nights for a full refund, and we cover the return postage. No photographs, no form to argue your case — one email.

settings.heading: Try it for 60 nights
settings.subheading: Use it every evening for two months. If your skin hasn't changed, send it back and we refund the full amount — return shipping included.
